activator
noun [ C ]
uk/ˈæk.tɪ.veɪ.tər/ us/ˈæk.tə.veɪ.t̬ɚ/
Add to word list Add to word list
something that causes a process or machine to start:
These classroom activities are useful as activators of language use for learning.
Insert the activator card into the voting machine.
chemistry   specialized
a substance that makes a chemical reaction happen more quickly:
The key ingredient in the fuel additive is an oxygen activator that makes the fuel burn more efficiently.
Leaves will rot down within 12 months if you use an activator on your compost heap.
biology   specialized
in genetics, a protein that increases the transcription (= the process in which a cell makes a copy of a particular piece of DNA) of a particular gene :
The repressor blocked the ability of the activator to "turn on" genes.
Allicin, a sulphur compound produced by crushing or chewing fresh garlic, was found to be an activator of TRPA1.
More examplesFewer examples
  • The cues serve as activators of the decision process for a purchase, making the customer more likely to buy.
  • The glue capsule comes with an activator that improves the adhesive bond.
  • The blood clotting system may be triggered by production of high levels of plasminogen activator.
  • The steroid receptor RNA activator protein is expressed in breast tumour tissues.
